source_text:
Καὶ ὅσοι μὲν ἐξ αἵματος
καθαροῦ τυγχάνουσιν, οὗτοί εἰσι πάντοτε χαίροντες καὶ παίζοντες καὶ γελῶντες, καὶ
εἰσὶν ἀνθηροὶ, καὶ καλόχρωοι· ὅσοι δὲ ἀπὸ χολῆς ξανθῆς τυγχάνουσιν, εἰσὶ γοργοὶ
καὶ εὔτολμοι, ὀργίλοι καὶ πικροὶ καὶ ἀλλόχρωοι· ὅσοι δὲ ἀπὸ χολῆς μελαίνης
τυγχάνουσιν, εἰσὶ ῥᾴθυμοι καὶ ὀλιγόψυχοι, φιλάσθενοι καὶ ὀκνηροὶ καὶ δειλοί· ὅσοι
δὲ ἀπὸ φλέγματος τυγχάνουσιν, εἰσὶ λυπηροὶ, καὶ μὴν καὶ ψυχροὶ, ἀμνήμονες καὶ
διαλελησμένοι, τὰ πολλὰ κοιμώμενοι, καὶ λευκόχρωοι. Καὶ ἐπὶ μὲν τῆς παιδικῆς
ἡλικίας τὸ αἷμα πληθύνεται ἕως ἐτῶν δεκατεσσάρων· ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν νεανίσκων ἡ χολὴ
ἡ ξανθὴ πληθύνεται, ἕως ἐτῶν εἴκοσι ὀκτώ· ἐπὶ δὲ τῆς τελείας ἡλικίας ἡ χολὴ ἡ
μελαίνη πληθύνεται, ἕως ἐτῶν τεσσαράκοντα δύο· ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν γερόντων τὸ φλέγμα
πληθύνεται, ἕως ἐτῶν ὀγδοήκοντα.
orientation: John of Damascus is explaining how each of the four humors produces a distinct temperament and dominates a successive stage of human life.
pass_a_gloss: And as many as happen to be from pure blood, these are always rejoicing and playing and laughing, and they are blooming and fair-complexioned. And as many as happen to be from yellow bile, they are quick and bold, irascible and bitter and of strange complexion. And as many as happen to be from black bile, they are sluggish and faint-hearted, sickly and lazy and cowardly. And as many as happen to be from phlegm, they are sorrowful, and indeed also cold, forgetful and utterly oblivious, sleeping most of the time, and pale-complexioned. And in childhood the blood increases until fourteen years. And in young men the yellow bile increases, until twenty-eight years. And in the prime of life the black bile increases, until forty-two years. And in old men the phlegm increases, until eighty years.

choices.why: The compound means 'other-colored'; 'strange complexion' preserves the sense of an abnormal or altered skin tone without modernizing to a specific color term.
The perfect participle of διαλανθάνω means 'having completely escaped notice' or 'utterly forgotten'; 'utterly oblivious' captures the intensive force of the prefix δια-.
The accusative of respect with the participle means 'sleeping for the most part'; this rendering keeps the adverbial force of τὰ πολλά.
The phrase means 'at the age of childhood'; 'in childhood' is the natural English equivalent while keeping the temporal sense of ἐπί with the genitive.
τελεία ἡλικία means 'complete/perfect age', i.e., maturity; 'prime of life' conveys the sense of full adulthood without the modern connotation of 'middle age'.

pass_b_english: Those who happen to be made of pure blood are always cheerful, playful, and laughing. They look fresh and have a fine complexion. Those who happen to be made of yellow bile are quick and bold, irascible, bitter, and have an unusual coloring. Those who happen to be made of black bile are sluggish and faint-hearted, sickly, hesitant, and timid. Those who happen to be made of phlegm are sorrowful and also cold, forgetful and utterly oblivious, sleeping most of the time, and pale-complexioned.

In childhood, blood increases until the age of fourteen. In youth, yellow bile increases until the age of twenty-eight. In the prime of life, black bile increases until the age of forty-two. In old age, phlegm increases until the age of eighty.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'καλόχρωοι' as 'ruddy complexion', not 'fine complexion'.
last_rejected.ruling: καλόχρωοι means fair/good complexion; 'fine' is within normal range, not a major error

polish.changed: I clarified the ambiguous phrase 'of strange complexion' as 'have an unusual coloring,' broke the long opening sentence into two for easier reading, and kept the paragraph break where the discussion shifts from temperaments to the stages of life.

notes.why: 'Strange complexion' is odd; likely means unusual or sallow coloring.
